prompts.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes or contributed to group efforts over time.

Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side.
What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
Describe how you have taken advantage of a significant educational opportunity or worked to overcome an educational barrier you have faced.
Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?
Think about an academic subject that inspires you. Describe how you have furthered this interest inside and/or outside of the classroom.
What have you done to make your school or your community a better place?
Beyond what has already been shared in your application, what do you believe makes you a strong candidate for admissions to the University of California?

intl_finance.document: Proof of funding for one academic year (F-1), submitted with the I-20 request e-form in iGlobal; UC Davis states acceptable funding includes personal and family funds and UC Davis guaranteed scholarships and fellowships

deadlines.label: I-20/DS-2019 requests open in iGlobal
deadlines.note: Beginning in April, after the Statement of Intent to Register and the SISS Pre-Arrival Orientation

intl_finance.notes: SISS (Services for International Students and Scholars) says you must be admitted and indicate you plan to attend before it can prepare the I-20. The exact list of documents and the dollar amount for new undergraduates is not published on the public pages read (it is inside the iGlobal e-form); ask SISS.

sources.title: UC Admissions: Personal insight questions (first-year; 4 of 8, max 350 words each)
UC Admissions: Presenting yourself on the first-year UC application 2026-27 (counselor guide)
UC Davis SISS: Student Visa & Entry into the United States
UC Davis SISS: Newly Admitted Students

notes: The 8 Personal Insight Questions are the same for all UC campuses (answer 4, max 350 words each); text copied from the UC Admissions page (source 1), which does not print a cycle year. Source 2 (UC counselor guide titled 2026-27) confirms the same format for the 2026-27 application: respond to 4 of the 8 questions, 350 words maximum per response. The UC application also has optional Additional comments boxes (source 2); they are not essay prompts and are not listed here. No UC Davis-specific written questions were found. For intl_finance, source 3 gives the timing (SIR, then I-20 request from April through iGlobal), source 4 states the F-1 funding rule, and source 5 says the I-20 e-form is available in iGlobal after the Pre-Arrival Orientation. The SISS site blocks automated downloads; the pages were read in a browser.
